title: Analysis: GlobalFoundries' calculus behind US$2 billion entry into TSMC's CoWoS ecosystem
key_facts: GlobalFoundries announced a multi-year manufacturing agreement with TSMC on 8 Oct 2026.
It will expand silicon interposer capacity at its Malta, New York fab for TSMC's CoWoS packaging.
Multiple media outlets put the five-year deal at about $2 billion.
Volume production is expected to ramp in the first half of 2028.
Interposers connect logic chips with high-bandwidth memory.
The deal covers interposers only, not chip assembly and testing, so overall CoWoS capacity stays constrained.
quote_evidence: GlobalFoundries (GF) has reached a multiyear manufacturing agreement with TSMC to expand silicon interposer capacity at its Malta fab in New York, supplying TSMC's Chip-on-Wafer-on-Substrate (CoWoS) advanced-packaging ecosystem...
However, the agreement primarily covers silicon interposer manufacturing and does not include full chip assembly and testing.
why_it_matters_hint: It adds a US source for a scarce AI packaging part but does not remove the wider packaging bottleneck.
notes: digitimes analysis is paywalled after the first sentence; details read from TradingKey. Deal itself is older than 14 Oct.
